This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $h(N)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ can be coloured with $k$ colours so that every four-term arithmetic progression must contain at least three distinct colours. Estimate $h(N)$. 
#160: [Er89]
additive combinatorics | 
arithmetic progressions
Investigated by Erdős and Freud. This has been discussed on MathOverflow, where LeechLattice shows\[h(N) \ll N^{2/3}.\]In the comments of this site Hunter improves this to\[h(N) \ll N^{\frac{\log 3}{\log 22}+o(1)}\](note $\frac{\log 3}{\log 22}\approx 0.355$).
The observation of Zach Hunter in that question coupled with recent progress on the size of subsets without three-term arithmetic progression (see [BlSi23] which improves slightly on the bounds due to Kelley and Meka [KeMe23]) imply that\[h(N) \gg \exp(c(\log N)^{1/9})\]for some $c>0$. 
Additional thanks to: Zach Hunter

 a better lower bound $h(N)\gg\exp\left(c(\log N)^{1/6-o(1)}\right)$ follows from the result in https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27045, which gives a new upper bound for the maximal subset of $[N]$ without 3-APs. To prevent a two-color 4-AP, you need to prevent a monochromatic 3-AP in the interval [N/4, 3N/4]. Thus the bound can be directly applied to this problem.
a better upper bound $h(N)\ll N^{1/4+o(1)}$ follows from a new construction in https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20752, details in the claimed partial proof.

 a better upper bound of $h(n) \ll N^{\log(3)/\log(22)+o(1)}$ follows from the methods in: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.06914. the point is, you can take products of Behrend-style colorings to get a $N^{o(1)}$-coloring which kills all patterns except the symmetric ABBA-pattern. and then by tensoring the explicit coloring at the bottom of page 2, you can use $O(N^{\log(3)/\log(22)})$ colors to kill ABBA. 
as the linked paper discusses, getting subpolynomial bounds on this ABBA problem would have implications for a conjecture of Ruzsa (see Theorem 1.7).

A partial proof 
claimed by Ruizhe Shi, Yiqi Dong (using GPT 5.6 Sol).
 Summary:
 We are not able to prove the $N^{o(1)}$ result. But this new result (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.20752) can improve the exponent in the upper bound from $\log_{22} 3$ to $1/4$. The approach is to give a new construction for the coloring problem introduced in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.06914. And the basic idea is to use the standard $\mathbb F_{p^3}/\mathbb F_p$ norm plus a linear term to color $\mathbb Z/p^4 \mathbb Z$. Then we can take a product of such a coloring with the Behrend-style coloring as previous comment suggested.

A partial proof 
claimed by Rio Itabe (using GPT-5.6).
 Summary:
 The claimed partial result is\[
h(N)\leq N^{1/3+o(1)},
\]which would improve the exponent \(\frac{\log 3}{\log 22}\) currently recorded on this page. Two \(N^{o(1)}\)-colour digit filters force every four-term progression receiving at most two colours from their product to have the proper \(ABBA\) pattern. A \(9p\)-colour carry-and-norm factor over \(\mathbf F_{p^3}\), with \(p=O(N^{1/3})\), excludes that remaining pattern.
